question: Which system changes caused the payment processing delays in March 2026, which services were affected, and which documents confirm this?
answer: The March 2026 payment‑processing delays were caused by two system changes. CHG‑2044 rolled out a new fraud‑scoring model (v3.3) that increased the fraud‑scoring p99 latency from about 80 ms to about 450 ms, creating a processing bottleneck [E4][E11]. CHG‑2041 reduced the payment‑gateway ledger‑db connection‑pool max size from 200 to 60 connections, which left insufficient connections to handle the longer‑lasting requests caused by the slower fraud‑scoring model [E4][E13][E15]. The combination of these changes caused card payments to be delayed or fail between 13:52 UTC and 16:40 UTC on 11 Mar 2026, affecting the Card Payments service and the Checkout API that routes those payments [E1][E5]. The incident is documented in the Kestrel Pay status page incident history (which lists the affected components and notes the rollback of the risk‑scoring change) [E1], the final postmortem “INC‑2026‑0311 – Card payment processing delays” (which details the two root‑cause changes and their interaction) [E4][E12][E10], the initial incident report “INC‑2026‑0311 – Card payment processing delays” (which describes the symptoms and timeline) [E5][E16], and the Q1 2026 change‑log entries for CHG‑2044 and CHG‑2041 (which record the rollout of the fraud model and the connection‑pool reduction) [E11][E13].

citations.text: Between 13:52 and 16:40 UTC on 2026-03-11, card payments were delayed or failed. Two changes combined to cause the incident. CHG-2041, made two days earlier, had reduced the payment-gateway database connection pool from 200 to 60 connections. Neither change caused problems on its own.

citations.title: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays
citations.section: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays > Root cause
citations.text:
payment-gateway holds a ledgerdb connection while it waits for the synchronous fraud-scoring call (known technical debt TD-112). The number of connections in use is therefore roughly the request rate multiplied by the time each request holds a connection.

At the afternoon peak of about 320 payments per second, with fraud-scoring at 450 ms, the gateway needed about 320 x 0.45 = 144 connections. The pool allowed 60 after CHG-2041, so requests queued until merchant-api timed out after 30 seconds.

citations.title: Incident Report INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays
citations.section: Incident Report INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays > Summary
citations.text: On 2026-03-11 card payments submitted through the Checkout API were delayed and some failed with timeout errors. The incident started at 14:05 UTC and was resolved at 16:40 UTC. Fraud-scoring latency was elevated after the fraud model v3.3 rollout earlier that day. The model was rolled back and the payment-gateway database connection pool was enlarged.

citations.title: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays
citations.section: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays > Root cause
citations.text:
Before CHG-2044, the same traffic needed about 320 x 0.08 = 26 connections, which fit within 60. With the original pool of 200, 144 connections would also have fit. The failure required both changes.

The v3.3 rollout went to 100% of traffic at 09:30 UTC without the canary stage required by the fraud model rollout runbook, so the latency regression was not caught before the afternoon peak.

citations.title: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays
citations.section: Postmortem INC-2026-0311 - Card payment processing delays > Resolution
citations.text:
15:20 UTC: fraud model rolled back to v3.2 (CHG-2047). fraud-scoring p99 returned to about 85 ms.

16:35 UTC: payment-gateway connection pool restored to 200 (CHG-2048).

16:40 UTC: incident resolved.

question: To what size was the payment-gateway connection pool raised during INC-2026-0311?
answer: During incident INC-2026-0311 the payment‑gateway connection pool was raised to a maximum size of **150** connections. This is recorded in the reliability review, which notes the pool was raised to 150 (CHG‑2048) and remained at that size [E2], and in the change‑log entry for CHG‑2048, which describes raising the ledgerdb connection pool max_size from 60 to 150 [E3].

citations.text:
INC-2026-0311 delayed 12,400 card payments, the largest impact this quarter. The gateway connection pool was raised to 150 during the incident (CHG-2048) and has stayed at 150.

Action item status as of 2026-04-06:

AI-1, pool saturation alert: Done.

AI-2, release the ledgerdb connection before calling fraud-scoring: In progress, scheduled for release as CHG-2055 on 2026-04-08.

AI-3, enforce the fraud model canary stage: Done on 2026-03-30.
